newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Richina suspends div reinvestment plan.
newsitem.headline: Richina suspends div reinvestment plan.

text.p: Leather and theme parks group Richina Pacific said on Thursday it had suspended its dividend reinvestment scheme.
When it announced its half year profits last month, Richina also launched a fully underwritten, renounceable one for two cash issue at NZ30 cents.
This was to be followed by a one-for-five share consolidation and a dividend for shares held before the rights issue allotment.

Richina said on Thursday it was suspending the reinvestment plan for the fully imputed 0.5 cent per share dividend (payable May 15), "in order to protect the interest of shareholders who had made a standing nomination to receive shares in the company in lieu of receiving a dividend".
Shareholders could choose whether they participated in the reinvestment plan, and many had made a standing nomination to accept shares instead, it explained.
"If such a nomination was implemented those shareholders would be paying a premium over the current market price for shares, which is clearly not in their own best interests," Richina said.
The directors have decided to scrap the plan. Instead, the May 15 dividend will be paid in cash on that day.
